requirements.desc: Every human user signs in to exactly one tenant context (or the vendor console); the session carries tenant id, user id, roles and assurance level, and no request is served without it.
requirements.why: Tenant isolation is a Critical gap; the client must never supply the tenant id.
requirements.pre: User account exists and is active in the tenant.
requirements.trigger: User opens the sign-in page or a session expires.
requirements.in: Email or SSO assertion; password or passkey; second factor when required.
requirements.logic: Verify credential at the identity provider; resolve tenant from the sign-in hostname; issue a short-lived access token and a rotating refresh token bound to the tenant; record an audit event.
requirements.valid: Account not locked; tenant active; clock skew within tolerance.
requirements.err: Wrong credential (generic message, counter incremented); locked account; tenant archived (read-only notice); IdP unavailable (retry page).
requirements.perm: Public endpoint; rate limited per IP and per account.
requirements.title: Tenant-scoped authentication and sessions

requirements.desc: Tenant admins, payout preparers and approvers, plan approvers, compliance officers and all vendor staff must pass a second factor; approvals require a fresh factor (step-up) within a configurable window.
requirements.why: Account takeover of an approver redirects money (threat T10).
requirements.persona: Tenant admin; Finance approver; Vendor ops
requirements.trigger: Sign-in, or an action flagged step-up (approve batch, commit run, activate plan, approve adjustment, change bank details).
requirements.logic: Deny privileged session without enrolled factor; for step-up actions require a factor verified within the step-up window; record assurance level on the approval record.
requirements.out: Session assurance level AAL2; approval records carry factor time.
requirements.valid: Factor enrolled; code unused; within window.
requirements.err: No factor enrolled (forced enrolment); invalid code (limited retries); lost device (admin-assisted reset is a logged case with second approver).
requirements.perm: Self-service enrolment; reset needs Tenant admin plus second approver.
requirements.title: Multi-factor authentication for privileged roles

requirements.desc: Permissions are granted through roles; each assignment can be scoped by market and brand; distributor-facing access is additionally scoped by downline relationship (see FR-GEN-006). Platform-defined base roles can be cloned into tenant roles.
requirements.why: UX requires role-specific navigation and the security model requires least privilege.
requirements.pre: Tenant admin signed in with MFA.
requirements.trigger: Admin creates a role, edits permissions or assigns a user.
requirements.in: Role name; permission set; scope (markets, brands); assignee.
requirements.logic: Validate against the permission catalogue; reject combinations that break separation of duties (FR-IAM-004); a grant of an admin or approver role opens an approval request for a second admin; all changes audited and effective immediately on approval.
requirements.out: Role, role assignment, audit events, alert on new admin role.
requirements.valid: Permission exists; scope values exist; assigner cannot grant permissions they do not hold.
requirements.err: Conflicting duty pair; sole remaining admin cannot remove own admin role.
requirements.perm: Tenant admin (grant of admin or approver role needs second admin).
requirements.title: Roles, permissions and attribute scopes

requirements.desc: The person who prepares a payout batch, a run commit, a plan activation or an adjustment cannot approve it; the rule is enforced in the service layer from recorded actor ids, not by role names alone.
requirements.why: No single person may release money or change pay rules.
requirements.pre: An approvable object exists with a recorded preparer.
requirements.in: Object id; approver identity; step-up factor.
requirements.logic: Compare approver with preparer and with all contributors to the object; refuse if equal; refuse if the approver is the beneficiary payee or a declared related party (adjustments); record the decision.
requirements.out: Approval record or refusal with reason code SOD-01.
requirements.valid: Approver holds the approval permission in scope.
requirements.err: Self-approval; no eligible approver available (delegation rule lists eligible users; never self-approval).
requirements.title: Separation of duties

requirements.desc: Vendor staff have no standing access to tenant data. Access is a request with reason and scope that a tenant admin approves for a fixed duration; sessions are read-only by default, region-bound, fully logged and visible to the tenant.
requirements.why: The platform concentrates many tenants' payout and personal data (threat T3). In MVP-A the vendor handles a design partner's export, so the control is needed from the first tenant.
requirements.pre: Vendor user has MFA; tenant has at least one admin.
requirements.in: Tenant; reason; scope (modules, read-only or named write action); duration.
requirements.logic: Create request; notify tenant admins; on approval mint a time-boxed scoped credential; log every screen view, query and API call to the tenant-visible session log; expire automatically; produce a session report.
requirements.out: Support session, session log, session report.
requirements.valid: Duration within tenant maximum; requester outside the tenant's region needs explicit region approval.
requirements.err: No decision before expiry of the request (auto-denied); attempted action outside scope (blocked and logged).
requirements.perm: Request: Vendor ops. Decide: Tenant admin.
requirements.title: Vendor support sessions

requirements.desc: Integrations authenticate with scoped, rotatable keys tied to a service account with its own role, rate limit and IP allow-list.
requirements.why: Commerce connectors and tenant systems write orders; mass extraction must be bounded (threat T11).
requirements.trigger: Admin creates or rotates a key.
requirements.in: Name; scopes; rate limit tier; allowed IP ranges; expiry.
requirements.logic: Generate key, show once, store only a hash; attach scopes; enforce per-key rate limits and pagination caps; rotation keeps the old key valid for a grace period.
requirements.valid: Scopes from the catalogue; no bulk personal-data scope without a stated purpose.
requirements.err: Expired or revoked key (401); scope missing (403); limit exceeded (429 with Retry-After).
requirements.title: API keys and service accounts

requirements.desc: Distributors sign in to the portal with email or phone one-time code or password, optional second factor, and re-authentication for sensitive changes.
requirements.why: The distributor population is large and varied; sign-in must work on low-end phones without weakening bank-detail controls.
requirements.pre: Participant with type flag can-earn has a verified contact.
requirements.logic: Issue portal session scoped to the participant and the positions they own; bank-detail and tax-profile changes require fresh re-authentication.
requirements.valid: Contact verified; participant not terminated (terminated participants keep read access to past statements for the retention period).
requirements.err: Unknown identifier (generic response); code expired.
requirements.title: Distributor sign-in

requirements.desc: A tenant is created with a data region, an isolation tier (pooled or dedicated database) and a routing entry; all tenant data, backups and exports stay in that region.
requirements.why: Residency duties and large tenants must be served without re-architecture.
requirements.in: Legal name; region; isolation tier; first admin contact.
requirements.logic: Create routing entry and database (or schema objects in the pooled database); apply row-level security policies; create first admin invitation; record DPA reference and breach contacts.
requirements.valid: Region available; tier allowed in region.
requirements.err: Provisioning step fails (idempotent retry; tenant stays in state Provisioning).
requirements.title: Tenant provisioning and data region

requirements.desc: A tenant defines brands and the markets it has opened; each market has a currency, time zone, language set, market pack reference and calendars with cut-off time zones.
requirements.why: Plans, orders, tax and compliance rules are market-scoped; the brand dimension is cheap now and costly later.
requirements.trigger: Admin adds or edits a market, brand or calendar.
requirements.in: Market code; currency; time zone; languages; calendar definitions.
requirements.logic: Store as a new settings version; calendars generate periods ahead; a market cannot be deleted once referenced.
requirements.valid: ISO currency and country codes; no overlapping periods within a calendar.
requirements.err: Change would alter a committed period (refused).
requirements.title: Markets, brands, currencies and calendars

requirements.desc: Tenant settings (rounding mode, clawback policy, visibility policy, thresholds, notice periods) are versioned and audited like plan versions; every run records the settings version it used.
requirements.why: A run must be reproducible; a silent settings change would break replay.
requirements.in: Setting key; new value; effective date; reason.
requirements.logic: Create a new immutable settings version effective from the date; settings that change money need a second approver.
requirements.valid: Value within platform bounds; effective date not inside a committed period.
requirements.err: Back-dated change (refused); missing approver.
requirements.perm: Tenant admin; money-affecting keys need Finance approver.
requirements.title: Versioned tenant settings

requirements.desc: A market can be switched to Live only when the checklist is complete: licence or registration evidence, payment and payout provider eligibility, tax rules, agreement versions, data region, plan variant.
requirements.why: Operating before a licence or without an eligible provider is a launch blocker.
requirements.trigger: Admin opens the checklist or requests go-live.
requirements.in: Evidence documents; provider approval record; tax configuration reference.
requirements.logic: Each item has an owner, evidence and status; go-live needs all mandatory items for that market pack plus compliance sign-off; enrolment and order ingestion for the market are blocked until Live.
requirements.valid: Evidence attached for each mandatory item; provider approval names the approved business description.
requirements.err: Missing item (blocked with list).
requirements.perm: Tenant admin prepares; Compliance officer signs off.
requirements.title: Market launch checklist

requirements.desc: A tenant can be moved to read-only archive after a final run and a complete export; data is retained per law and then deleted.
requirements.why: Distributors and regulators may need records after a tenant closes.
requirements.in: Final period; export destination; retention basis.
requirements.logic: Run final period; produce full export; switch to archive; schedule deletion.
requirements.valid: No open payout batches.
requirements.err: Open obligations (listed).
requirements.title: Tenant archive and offboarding

requirements.desc: A design partner's back-office export (participants, orders, payout lines) is uploaded as files and validated against the published schema before any row is stored.
requirements.why: MVP-A reads an operator's existing data; it must refuse personal or bank data it does not need.
requirements.trigger: User uploads files or drops them in the tenant's inbound location.
requirements.in: Three CSV files; declared period range; market; currency.
requirements.logic: Check required columns, types, key uniqueness and referential links; reject files containing columns that look like names, contacts, addresses, identity or bank data; compute row counts and control totals; store the batch in state Validated or Rejected with a row-level error report.
requirements.valid: Participant ids pseudonymous; amounts are integers in minor units; months in range; every order buyer and payout payee exists.
requirements.err: Schema mismatch; forbidden column present; orphan references above tolerance; duplicate keys.
requirements.title: Export upload and schema validation

requirements.desc: The partner's own codes are mapped to the platform vocabulary: participant types to flags (earns, counts as end customer), order purpose, payout source kind, starter-kit flag. A mapping is versioned and every report records the mapping version.
requirements.why: Retail share depends on which types count as customers; the mapping is a judgement that must be visible.
requirements.logic: List distinct source values with counts; require a target for each; unmapped values default to unknown and are reported; saving creates a new mapping version.
requirements.valid: Every source value mapped or explicitly left unknown.
requirements.err: Mapping changed after a snapshot was published (new snapshot required; old one keeps its version).
requirements.title: Value mapping with versions

requirements.desc: Batches move Uploaded, Validated, Mapped, Loaded, Superseded; loading writes compliance facts; a data-quality report states coverage and unknowns.
requirements.why: Reports on poor data must say so.
requirements.logic: Load into compliance fact tables in one transaction per batch; re-import of the same period supersedes the earlier batch without deleting it; compute share of orders with unknown purpose, refunds without month, payout lines without source order.
requirements.valid: Control totals after load equal totals at validation.
requirements.err: Load interrupted (transaction rolled back; batch stays Mapped).
requirements.title: Import batch lifecycle and data-quality report

requirements.desc: Instead of files, facts are pulled from the partner's back office through read-only SQL access on a schedule.
requirements.why: Incumbents expose SQL access; removes manual export. Unvalidated demand.
requirements.in: Connection reference; query templates per vendor.
requirements.logic: Run parameterised read-only queries; land rows as a batch; same validation as files.
requirements.valid: Queries return only schema columns.
requirements.err: Connection refused; schema drift.
requirements.title: Read-only database connector

requirements.desc: Per period: net sales, share bought by participant types flagged as end customers, share including declared resale, starter-kit share, and share of participant orders with unknown purpose.
requirements.why: The share of sales to non-participants is the number regulators look at; no vendor material read computes it from transaction data.
requirements.trigger: User requests a snapshot for a period range.
requirements.in: Period range; market; mapping or settings version.
requirements.logic: Net sales = amount minus refunded amount per order; numerator = orders whose buyer type counts as end customer; second figure adds participant orders with purpose resale; all figures stored with population counts and method version.
requirements.out: Report snapshot with figures and method notes.
requirements.valid: Denominator not zero, otherwise figure is null with reason.
requirements.err: Facts superseded during computation (snapshot aborted, retried).
requirements.title: Retail-customer share report (R1)

requirements.desc: Of the order volume on which multi-level pay was earned in a period, the share from orders tagged personal use and the share with unknown purpose; plus the count of payees whose multi-level pay from personal-use volume exceeds a tenant threshold.
requirements.why: Makes a one-third style test computable; the threshold is the tenant's counsel's, not the platform's.
requirements.pre: Payout lines carry source order references.
requirements.logic: Select positive payout lines of source kind downline volume; sum volume of their distinct source orders by purpose; per payee compare pay from personal-use orders with the threshold share of that payee's multi-level pay.
requirements.valid: Lines without a source order are counted and reported as unattributable.
requirements.err: Threshold not set (figure shown, flag count omitted).
requirements.title: Personal-use share of rewarded volume (R2)

requirements.desc: Per period and per year: gross payouts by source kind (retail sale, downline volume, enrolment order, pool, match, other) and clawbacks shown separately.
requirements.why: Shows what money was paid for, the basis of the "derived primarily from introducing others" analysis.
requirements.pre: Payout lines classified by source kind.
requirements.logic: Sum amounts by source kind excluding clawbacks for shares; report clawbacks as a separate negative total; shares sum to 100 within rounding.
requirements.valid: Every line has a source kind (unknown allowed, reported).
requirements.err: None specific.
requirements.title: Payout source mix (R3)

requirements.desc: Per period: distributors active under the plan's own-purchase rule, the share of them with no customer order, and orders placed on or after a configurable day that lift the buyer across a rank threshold, with how many were later refunded.
requirements.why: Purchases to qualify and period-end buying are named indicators; they need operational definitions.
requirements.in: Active threshold; rank thresholds; late-order day.
requirements.logic: Accumulate personal volume per distributor in day order; detect crossings by late orders; join refunds.
requirements.valid: Thresholds present.
requirements.err: Missing day field in orders (indicator omitted with note).
requirements.title: Qualification-by-purchase and period-end threshold orders (R4)

requirements.desc: For a year: every participant who held an earning agreement at any time, including those who earned nothing; share earning more than zero, mean, median, percentiles, bands. Basis stated as gross commissions net of clawbacks, before expenses.
requirements.why: Disclosures must reflect the typical participant; this is the internal computation that a published disclosure (FR-CPL-009) later uses.
requirements.pre: A full year of payout lines.
requirements.logic: Population = earning-type participants enrolled on or before year end; earnings = sum of payout lines per participant, zero when none; compute statistics; band counts sum to the population.
requirements.valid: Population count equals band total.
requirements.err: Partial year (labelled partial; not publishable).
requirements.title: Earnings distribution over all participants (R5)

requirements.desc: Each report run is an immutable snapshot recording inputs (batch ids or run ids), mapping or settings version, method version, figures and populations. Any figure can be opened to its population and source rows.
requirements.why: A compliance figure that cannot be reproduced or explained is not evidence.
requirements.trigger: Snapshot creation or a figure is opened.
requirements.logic: Compute in a job; store figures with keys; drill-down query returns the rows that formed numerator and denominator, paginated, export logged.
requirements.valid: Recomputing a snapshot from the same inputs and versions gives identical figures.
requirements.err: Inputs superseded (snapshot marked Outdated, never changed).
requirements.title: Report snapshots, method versions and drill-down

requirements.desc: Platform-level rules, separate from tenant plan rules, evaluate plan configurations and fee configurations per market with one of three outcomes: blocked, warned and logged, or reported.
requirements.why: Decides whether the platform helps configure an unlawful plan; default stance Moderate pending founder and counsel.
requirements.pre: Market pack loaded with guardrail rules and their basis status.
requirements.trigger: Plan version saved, submitted or activated; fee configured.
requirements.logic: Evaluate each guardrail predicate over the declarative configuration; blocked outcomes refuse save with rule id and explanation; warned outcomes require acknowledgement; every decision stored immutably.
requirements.valid: Rule has a basis status; counsel-required rules marked provisional until confirmed.
requirements.err: Extension module opaque to predicates (treated as warned, routed to compliance review).
requirements.perm: System; visible to Plan administrator and Compliance officer.
requirements.title: Platform guardrails

requirements.desc: Where platform policy permits an override, the tenant records a written justification and approver; overrides appear in compliance reports and in the vendor's tenant review.
requirements.why: Overrides must be visible, not silent.
requirements.pre: A warned or overridable decision exists.
requirements.logic: Only outcomes marked overridable can be overridden; needs Compliance officer approval; blocked-by-law outcomes are never overridable.
requirements.valid: Justification present.
requirements.err: Not overridable (refused).
requirements.title: Guardrail overrides log

requirements.desc: A disclosure document is generated from an R5 snapshot, reviewed, published with a version and kept with its method and data references for the retention period.
requirements.why: Substantiation on demand if the US proposal is adopted; trust feature elsewhere.
requirements.logic: Draft, review, publish; published versions immutable; public page shows the current version; statements link to it.
requirements.valid: Snapshot is full-year and not outdated.
requirements.err: Snapshot outdated (blocked).
requirements.title: Earnings disclosure publication and substantiation

requirements.desc: Documented, configurable signals with tenant thresholds: period-end threshold orders, returns after qualification, shared payment fingerprints or addresses between a distributor and their customers.
requirements.why: Bonus buying and fake customers need measurable definitions; signals are indicators, never findings.
requirements.logic: Compute signals; list flags with evidence; open cases on request.
requirements.valid: Each flag labelled as indicator.
requirements.err: Missing attributes (signal disabled with note).
requirements.title: Integrity signals

requirements.desc: Versioned approved claims per market and the current disclosure figures are exposed by API and webhook to claims-monitoring partners.
requirements.why: Claims on social media are frequent; monitoring is integrated, not built.
requirements.logic: Store versions; emit change events.
requirements.valid: Claim linked to a disclosure where it mentions earnings.
requirements.err: None specific.
requirements.title: Approved-claims catalogue and disclosure feed

requirements.desc: Every market-pack rule (guardrail, tax, cooling-off, filing) stores its basis and basis status: screening, primary read, or counsel-confirmed, with source reference and review date.
requirements.why: Legal content is screening-grade until counsel confirms; the product must not present it as settled.
requirements.logic: Status shown wherever the rule is applied; a market cannot go Live with mandatory rules still at screening status unless the tenant accepts the risk in writing.
requirements.valid: Status in the allowed set.
requirements.err: Go-live with screening-status mandatory rule (blocked or risk acceptance recorded).
requirements.perm: Vendor ops maintains packs; Compliance officer accepts.
requirements.title: Rule basis status in configuration

requirements.desc: Where a market pack requires them: grievance register with response-time tracking and a publishable delisted-seller register.
requirements.why: Reported duties in India; included only when that pack is activated and confirmed.
requirements.pre: Market pack with the register enabled.
requirements.logic: Grievances run on the case framework with market deadlines; delisted register is a published view of terminated participants per the pack's rule.
requirements.valid: Deadlines from the pack.
requirements.err: Deadline near (escalation).
requirements.title: Market-pack registers

requirements.desc: A participant is a person or entity known to the tenant. Types are tenant-defined with flags (can earn, counts as end customer, can sponsor, can hold positions); a participant's type is effective-dated and a change never re-labels past orders.
requirements.why: Real plans have affiliates, preferred customers, promoters and builders; retail share depends on the flags.
requirements.in: External id; type; market; identity references; contact data.
requirements.logic: Create participant; type assignment rows with valid-from and valid-to; sensitive documents go to the separate encrypted store.
requirements.valid: External id unique per tenant; market Live; one active type at any time.
requirements.err: Duplicate suspicion (FR-PAR-003); market not Live.
requirements.perm: Support agent creates; type definitions by Tenant admin with Compliance officer approval.
requirements.title: Participant record and effective-dated participant types

requirements.desc: Enrolments arrive by API or connector; an enrolment is accepted only for a Live market the participant is resident in, and creates the participant, an initial position where the type holds positions, and sponsor and placement relationships.
requirements.why: A distributor enrolling someone in an unopened market creates legal exposure.
requirements.pre: Sponsor position exists and is active.
requirements.in: Participant data; sponsor reference; placement preference; agreement version accepted.
requirements.logic: Validate market; run duplicate checks; create records in one transaction; household rule check where the plan declares one.
requirements.valid: Sponsor can sponsor; placement target valid for the plan.
requirements.err: Market closed (422 MARKET_NOT_LIVE); sponsor inactive; placement slot taken (retry with deterministic alternative).
requirements.perm: API key scope enrol; Support agent.
requirements.title: Enrolment intake with market gating

requirements.desc: New and changed participants are compared on identity reference, payment fingerprint, address and device signals; matches create a duplicate case and, where the tenant enables it, hold activation or payouts until reviewed.
requirements.why: Multiple accounts are legitimate in some plans and abuse in others; decisions need a trail.
requirements.trigger: Enrolment, bank-detail change or scheduled sweep.
requirements.logic: Deterministic matching rules with tenant thresholds; outcome merge, allow with reason, or terminate; history stays on positions.
requirements.valid: Hash comparison only; raw payment data never stored.
requirements.err: Merge would create a cycle or double ownership conflict (blocked).
requirements.perm: Support agent investigates; Compliance officer decides.
requirements.title: Duplicate-account detection queue

requirements.desc: Individual, joint and business-entity accounts; succession, divorce division and sale are transfers of position ownership with documents, approval and an effective date.
requirements.why: Transfers move future income; needs counsel per market.
requirements.in: Position; new owner; documents; effective date.
requirements.logic: Case with legal check; new ownership row; new payee needs tax profile and bank details under change controls.
requirements.valid: New owner eligible.
requirements.err: Missing documents.
requirements.title: Account types and ownership transfer

requirements.desc: Statuses Pending, Active, Suspended, Terminated, with reinstatement as an event on the same position; each change is dated with reason and actor.
requirements.why: Termination and reinstatement drive pay eligibility and must not rewrite history.
requirements.in: New status; effective date; reason; evidence.
requirements.logic: Append status row; termination for cause needs a human approver; open payouts follow tenant policy (hold or pay); customers reassigned (FR-CRM-002).
requirements.valid: Effective date not before last committed period end unless handled as correction.
requirements.err: Back-dated termination into committed period (routed to restatement policy).
requirements.title: Participant and position status lifecycle

requirements.desc: The tenant's distributor agreement and policy documents are versioned per market; each participant's acceptance is recorded with version and time.
requirements.why: Written agreements are required in several markets (candidate requirement, to confirm per pack).
requirements.trigger: Enrolment or new version requiring re-acceptance.
requirements.logic: Store acceptance; re-acceptance campaigns tracked.
requirements.valid: Version current for the market.
requirements.err: Acceptance missing at enrolment (blocked where the pack requires).
requirements.title: Agreement versions and acceptance records

requirements.desc: The tree is made of positions. A participant may own one or more positions; ownership is effective-dated; volume and qualification are evaluated per position unless the plan version says per participant.
requirements.why: Plans give several business centres per person; node equals person breaks them.
requirements.trigger: Enrolment or plan rule grants a position.
requirements.logic: Create position with ownership row; statements roll positions up per owner.
requirements.valid: Plan's limit on positions per participant.
requirements.err: Limit exceeded.
requirements.perm: System on enrolment; Support agent by case.
requirements.title: Positions separate from participants

requirements.desc: Sponsor and placement are separate relationship kinds, each row carrying valid time and recorded time; rows are never updated in place; at any valid time a child has at most one parent per kind and no cycles exist.
requirements.why: Reproducibility, disputes and audit depend on knowing what the tree was when a period was calculated.
requirements.in: Kind; parent; child; valid-from; event reference.
requirements.logic: Change closes the current row at the effective date and inserts a new one; correction supersedes the old row (recorded time) and inserts the corrected row with the original valid date; cycle and uniqueness checks run inside the transaction under a per-tree lock.
requirements.valid: No cycle; no overlap of valid ranges for the same child and kind among non-superseded rows.
requirements.err: Cycle (409 GEN_CYCLE); overlap; parent not in same tenant and tree.
requirements.perm: Only through enrolment or an approved case.
requirements.title: Effective-dated sponsor and placement relationships

requirements.desc: Staff can view any subtree as of a valid date and optionally as known at a past recorded time; runs reference the recorded-time instant they used.
requirements.why: Explaining a past payout after later corrections.
requirements.trigger: User selects dates in the explorer or opens a run's tree.
requirements.in: Root position; as-of date; known-at time; depth.
requirements.logic: Query non-superseded-as-of-known-at rows valid at the date; lazy by depth.
requirements.valid: Dates not in the future for known-at.
requirements.err: Read model rebuilding (served from the system of record with a notice, depth-limited).
requirements.title: Tree as of a date and as known at a time

requirements.desc: Sponsor or placement changes and corrections are requested as cases with reason and evidence, checked against the plan's change windows, reviewed, and applied with an effective date (change) or original date (correction, listing affected committed periods).
requirements.why: A genealogy change moves future income between people.
requirements.trigger: Agent or distributor files a request.
requirements.in: Position; kind; proposed parent; change or correction; dates; evidence.
requirements.logic: Policy check (window, approvals); simulate cycle and occupancy; for corrections compute affected committed periods and estimated payout impact; on approval apply through FR-GEN-002 and route affected periods to the restatement policy.
requirements.out: Case; relationship rows; notifications; read-model rebuild job.
requirements.valid: Evidence attached; proposed parent valid.
requirements.err: Outside window (rejected or exception route if the plan allows); would create a cycle; target leg occupied; affects committed period (flag, FL-07).
requirements.perm: Support agent files; Compliance officer approves.
requirements.title: Genealogy change and correction cases

requirements.desc: Automatic placement and spillover place a new position in a deterministic slot; concurrent enrolments into the same leg are serialised and the tie-break recorded.
requirements.why: Two people must not land in one slot. Priority depends on the segment decision; binary appeared in 4 of 16 hold-out plans.
requirements.pre: Plan declares a placement tree with width.
requirements.logic: Take a lock on the target leg; find the slot by the plan's rule; insert; release.
requirements.valid: Slot free at commit.
requirements.err: Lock timeout (retry).
requirements.title: Serialised placement for binary and matrix plans

requirements.desc: A tenant policy states which fields a viewer may see at which depth and relationship (for example name and rank to depth n, contact data only for personally sponsored, aggregates beyond); the API returns only permitted fields and never reveals the existence of positions outside the viewer's downline.
requirements.why: Genealogy views are the largest personal-data exposure surface.
requirements.trigger: Any distributor-facing genealogy or team request.
requirements.logic: Authorise by path read model (viewer is ancestor of target, depth d); apply the field matrix; aggregate beyond the depth limit; rate limit and log exports.
requirements.valid: Policy version recorded on response logs.
requirements.err: Target outside downline (404, same as not found).
requirements.perm: Policy edited by Tenant admin with DPO approval.
requirements.title: Downline visibility policy enforced on the server

requirements.desc: Explorers open on search and a focused node, expand lazily, cap depth and breadth per request, and show counts for collapsed branches.
requirements.why: Trees with thousands of nodes cannot be drawn whole.
requirements.persona: Support agent; Commission analyst; Team leader
requirements.pre: Read model current or marked stale.
requirements.logic: Search by id, name (staff), rank; subtree counts from the read model; breadcrumbs to root.
requirements.valid: Page size limits.
requirements.err: Stale read model banner.
requirements.perm: Staff per role; distributors per FR-GEN-006.
requirements.title: Search-first genealogy explorer

requirements.desc: A materialised-path read model per tree kind supports ancestor tests and subtree search; it is rebuilt asynchronously from the relationship rows after changes and is marked stale meanwhile.
requirements.why: Interactive authorisation checks must not run recursive queries on deep trees.
requirements.logic: Recompute paths for the moved subtree in batches; version the read model; switch atomically.
requirements.valid: Path count equals active position count.
requirements.err: Rebuild failure (retry; views keep stale notice; authorisation falls back to system-of-record check).
requirements.title: Path read model and rebuild

requirements.desc: Termination changes status only. Compression, roll-up, breakaway and dynamic generations are calculation-time behaviours of a plan version; re-parenting of a terminated position's downline, where a plan requires it, is a dated change event generated by a stated rule.
requirements.why: Mixing structure and calculation loses history or pays wrongly.
requirements.logic: Calculation applies behaviours as pure functions of snapshot and plan; rule-generated genealogy events go through the same event path as approved cases, with the rule id as approver.
requirements.valid: Behaviours named per bonus.
requirements.err: None specific.
requirements.title: Structure is never changed to implement a pay rule

requirements.desc: Orders, order lines and customers are upserted through a public API and webhooks from the tenant's commerce system; each write carries an idempotency key and source system id.
requirements.why: Commerce is integrated, not built; duplicates and retries are normal.
requirements.pre: API key with scope orders:write; market Live.
requirements.in: Source order id; buyer reference; lines (product, quantity, price, tax); payment status; event times; attribution hint; purpose.
requirements.logic: Deduplicate on tenant, source system, source id; resolve buyer and attribution; compute volumes per line from the product volume map effective at the crediting event time; fix buyer type, purpose, attribution and volumes on the order; assign to period by the crediting event rule; emit OrderIngested.
requirements.out: Order with lines; 200 on replay with the same body, 409 on same key with different body.
requirements.valid: Totals equal sum of lines; currency equals market currency (MVP single currency); buyer exists or is created as customer.
requirements.err: Unknown product (order held in exception queue); period committed (late queue, FR-ORD-005); market not Live.
requirements.title: Order ingestion API with idempotency

requirements.desc: Packaged connectors subscribe to order, refund and customer events, map fields to the ingestion API, pass attribution from link or code, and expose sync status.
requirements.why: The two most common commerce platforms behind which the engine can sit.
requirements.logic: Verify signatures; transform; call ingestion; nightly reconciliation of counts and totals; backfill by date range.
requirements.valid: Signature valid.
requirements.err: Store API limit (backoff); mapping gap (exception queue).
requirements.title: Shopify and WooCommerce connectors

requirements.desc: Every participant order carries a purpose (resale, personal use, unspecified) where the market or tenant requires it; buyer type, purpose, attribution and line volumes are fixed at ingestion and later master-data changes do not alter them.
requirements.why: Reports and commissions must not be recomputed from current master data.
requirements.logic: Store facts; corrections arrive as new order events with reason, not edits.
requirements.valid: Purpose in vocabulary.
requirements.err: Purpose required but missing (stored as unspecified and counted in data-quality figures).
requirements.title: Purpose tag and fixed order facts

requirements.desc: Return events reference order lines and carry amounts and volume effects per line; an exchange flagged as equal value does not reverse and re-credit volume; chargebacks are treated like refunds for volume and pay; cooling-off and buy-back windows come from the market pack.
requirements.why: Each case changes volume and therefore pay.
requirements.in: Order line references; quantities; refund amount; restocking fee; event type.
requirements.logic: Create order event; compute volume reversal per line; if the original period is open adjust inputs, otherwise create a late transaction for the reversal policy (FR-FIN-003).
requirements.out: Order event; late transaction when applicable.
requirements.valid: Returned quantity not above purchased minus already returned.
requirements.err: Unknown order (held for retry until order arrives; alert after timeout).
requirements.title: Returns, refunds, chargebacks and exchanges

requirements.desc: Any order or order event whose crediting time falls in a committed period is queued; by default its effect posts as an adjustment in the current open period with a link to the original period.
requirements.why: Committed periods stay reproducible while late facts are not lost.
requirements.logic: Queue with original period, effect estimate and proposed handling (adjust or restatement request); analyst can accept default in bulk with preview.
requirements.out: Late transaction; adjustment inputs for the open run.
requirements.valid: Linked original period exists.
requirements.err: None specific.
requirements.title: Late-transaction queue

requirements.desc: Renewal succeeded, failed, cancelled, disputed, dispute won or lost are consumed from the commerce platform and drive volume and commission effects.
requirements.why: Autoship volume often drives qualification.
requirements.logic: Map to order events; consent records stay with the merchant of record.
requirements.valid: Reference known.
requirements.err: Unknown reference.
requirements.title: Subscription and dispute events

requirements.desc: Each customer has at most one serviced-by position at a time, effective-dated; attribution of an order is decided at ingestion from link, code, enrolment or servicing relationship by the tenant's precedence rule and stored on the order.
requirements.why: Who a customer belongs to decides who is paid.
requirements.trigger: First order, link visit recorded by commerce, or manual assignment.
requirements.logic: Apply precedence; write servicing row; fractional roll-ups are plan parameters applied at calculation.
requirements.valid: One active servicer.
requirements.err: Conflict between two claims (case opened with attribution report).
requirements.title: Customer servicing relationship and attribution

requirements.desc: When a servicing position is terminated its customers are reassigned by the tenant rule (sponsor, company or customer choice) with an effective date and optional notice; past orders keep their attribution.
requirements.why: Customers keep being served and attribution stays correct.
requirements.logic: Close servicing rows; open new ones; notify.
requirements.valid: Target eligible.
requirements.err: No eligible target (assigned to company).
requirements.perm: System by rule; Support agent overrides by case.
requirements.title: Customer reassignment on termination

requirements.desc: A distributor keeps private contacts and follow-up reminders; prospect data is private to that distributor by default.
requirements.why: Small native feature tied to attribution; controllership needs counsel.
requirements.pre: Counsel view on controllership for the market.
requirements.logic: Store scoped to the distributor; retention timer; deletion on request.
requirements.valid: Consent before marketing messages.
requirements.err: None specific.
requirements.title: Distributor contacts and reminders

requirements.desc: A plan has versions with states Draft, In review, Approved, Scheduled, Active, Retired; an activated version is immutable; each version has an effective date, approver, justification, transition rules and per-market filing status.
requirements.why: A run uses exactly one plan version; changes need a record of who approved what and why.
requirements.pre: Plan exists for brand and market.
requirements.trigger: Admin creates or edits a draft.
requirements.logic: Validate schema and references; guardrail evaluation on save; version diff available at every state.
requirements.valid: Effective date at a period boundary of each calendar the plan uses.
requirements.err: Guardrail blocked; validation errors listed per rule.
requirements.perm: Plan administrator edits; Compliance officer and second approver approve.
requirements.title: Plan versions

requirements.desc: Rules are composed from versioned primitives: volume measures per order line with item rules; hierarchy selector; qualification predicates including counts and profile facts; rank ladders with paid-as, title, maintenance and grace; payout functions (percent by level, generations with compression, differential, override, matching, fast start, flat, pool by shares); limits; carry state; calendars.
requirements.why: The most common mechanisms in the 21-plan corpus must be configuration, not code.
requirements.in: Primitive type; parameters; scope (market, participant types, bonus name).
requirements.logic: Typed parameter validation; dependency graph between rules determines pass order; plain-language rendering of each rule.
requirements.valid: No dependency cycle; every bonus names the tree and the volume measure it uses and its reversal policy.
requirements.err: Unknown measure; cyclic dependency.
requirements.title: Declarative primitive library

requirements.desc: Mechanisms outside the primitives are expressed first in a pure, typed expression language (no I/O, bounded evaluation) and, where that is insufficient, as platform-reviewed plan modules shipped in the platform codebase, versioned, parameterised and available to all tenants. Tenant-specific code branches are not allowed.
requirements.why: 11 of 16 hold-out plans need at least one mechanism outside any fixed list.
requirements.pre: Mechanism documented with examples from the plan document.
requirements.trigger: A rule cannot be expressed with primitives.
requirements.in: Expression or module reference with parameters; golden cases.
requirements.logic: Expressions are type-checked and evaluated deterministically; modules require golden tests and vendor code review before release; both are versioned and recorded in traces.
requirements.valid: At least one golden case per extension rule.
requirements.err: Type error; evaluation bound exceeded.
requirements.perm: Implementation consultant authors expressions; modules by vendor release only.
requirements.title: Controlled extension point

requirements.desc: A cap has scope (set of bonus types), base expression, rate, method (proportional, priority list, per person) and residue rule; per-participant constraints are evaluated before company-level caps. Pools have a base scoped by market and an allocation rule (shares, rank-ordered, first-N).
requirements.why: Two readings of one cap moved 9,130.43 between leader groups in the stress test.
requirements.trigger: Admin configures a cap or pool.
requirements.in: Scope; base; rate; method; priority order; residue rule.
requirements.logic: Validate scope bonuses exist; preview on a chosen historical period shows payees affected and amounts removed.
requirements.valid: Priority list covers the scope; residue rule set.
requirements.err: Scope overlaps another cap without stated precedence.
requirements.title: Caps and pools configuration

requirements.desc: A draft version is run on historical input snapshots without touching live results; the comparison shows per-payee and per-bonus differences against the current version, distribution of gains and losses, cap effects and guardrail flags, with totals reconciling to each run.
requirements.why: Table stakes for credibility; activation is blocked without it.
requirements.pre: At least one committed period or imported history snapshot.
requirements.logic: Worker job using the same engine code path with a simulation flag; results stored separately; diff computed in the database.
requirements.valid: Period is a full historical period.
requirements.err: Snapshot missing (cannot simulate).
requirements.title: Simulation and version comparison

requirements.desc: Frozen inputs with expected payout lines are kept per plan version and per platform primitive; every engine release and every plan version must reproduce them exactly.
requirements.why: Deterministic proof that a rule does what the plan document says.
requirements.pre: Examples from the plan document or a parallel run.
requirements.logic: Run and compare line by line; failures block activation and release.
requirements.valid: Expected totals equal sum of expected lines.
requirements.err: Mismatch listed per line.
requirements.title: Golden datasets

requirements.desc: A version moves through draft, simulation, compliance review with guardrails, filing status per market, field notice and effective date; activation is blocked without a full-period simulation and, where the market pack requires a filing, without recorded filing status.
requirements.why: A change that silently wipes accrued state is a dispute and possibly a legal issue.
requirements.in: Simulation reference; filing evidence; notice date.
requirements.logic: Checklist per market; second-person approval; scheduled activation at period boundary; notice period from tenant setting.
requirements.valid: All checklist items complete.
requirements.err: Missing simulation; missing filing status; notice period not met.
requirements.perm: Compliance officer approves; a second approver activates.
requirements.title: Plan-change governance

requirements.desc: Each new version declares how titles, carry balances, streak counters, banked points and one-time flags move from the previous version; a transition report lists every participant whose state changed.
requirements.why: Real plans carry long-horizon state that a change would otherwise cut.
requirements.logic: Apply transition functions as the first step of the first run under the new version; store before and after.
requirements.valid: Every state item has a declared rule (carry, map, reset with reason).
requirements.err: Undeclared item (activation blocked).
requirements.title: Transition rules between versions

requirements.desc: Each period of each calendar has a state: Open, Calculating, Calculated, Committed, Paid, Closed. Inputs and outputs are frozen at Committed. A transaction is assigned to a period by its crediting event and the calendar's cut-off time zone.
requirements.why: Without a lifecycle a late order either silently changes paid history or is lost.
requirements.logic: State machine with guarded transitions; Calculated is re-runnable and disposable; Committed requires approval; Paid when all batches for the period are settled or resolved; Closed after reconciliation sign-off.
requirements.out: Period state; events PeriodCutOff, PeriodCommitted, PeriodClosed.
requirements.valid: Transition allowed from current state; ingestion sync healthy before Calculating.
requirements.err: Sync behind (calculation blocked with last sync time); illegal transition (409).
requirements.perm: Commission analyst operates; Finance approver commits.
requirements.title: Calendars and period lifecycle

requirements.desc: A run binds one period, one plan version, one settings version and one input snapshot (orders, order events, genealogy as known at an instant, prior qualification state). It executes on a worker pool, is idempotent per run request id and locked per tenant, calendar and period.
requirements.why: Two analysts pressing run, or a retry, must not create two results.
requirements.pre: Period at cut-off, state Open or Calculated.
requirements.in: Period; run request id; plan version (by effective date).
requirements.logic: Acquire advisory lock; write snapshot reference; load tree and facts into memory; calculate; write result lines, qualification state candidates and control totals in one transaction; release lock; progress reported.
requirements.out: Run in state Calculated with totals; duplicate request returns the same run id.
requirements.valid: Plan version active for the period; snapshot complete.
requirements.err: Worker crash (run marked Failed; resumable from snapshot; no partial results visible); lock held (returns the running run id).
requirements.title: Run execution with snapshot, lock and idempotency

requirements.desc: Passes run in a fixed order: volumes per line and per position; qualification and paid-as rank; individual bonuses; matching; pools; per-participant constraints; caps; netting of clawbacks; minimums; rounding once per payout line; withholding.
requirements.why: Matching depends on others' bonuses, pools on company volume, caps on everything before them.
requirements.logic: Topological order of rule dependencies inside each pass; high-precision arithmetic until the rounding pass; allocation by largest remainder where a total is split.
requirements.out: Result lines with pass and rule ids.
requirements.valid: Engine invariants: lines sum to run total; caps not exceeded; allocations sum to their totals.
requirements.err: Invariant breach (run fails; nothing committed).
requirements.title: Multi-pass calculation order

requirements.desc: Per position and period the engine stores paid-as rank, highest title per ladder, counters, streaks, carry balances, banked points and one-time flags. State is an output of a committed run and an input to the next; it is never edited directly.
requirements.why: Rank is the main driver of pay; mutable fields make disputes unprovable.
requirements.pre: Prior committed state or migration import.
requirements.logic: Candidate state written with the run; becomes authoritative at commit; corrections only through restatement or migration import with approval.
requirements.valid: One row per position, period, calendar.
requirements.err: Missing prior state (period cannot be calculated; migration required).
requirements.perm: System; read by staff and by the owner.
requirements.title: Qualification state across periods

requirements.desc: Before commit the analyst sees totals against the previous run, variance by bonus type, top movers, exception list (invariant warnings, guardrail warnings, held payees, unusually large lines) and what changed in inputs and plan version.
requirements.why: A wrong approval pays thousands of people.
requirements.logic: Deterministic diff queries; thresholds for exceptions from tenant settings.
requirements.valid: Totals equal control totals of the run.
requirements.err: Sync became stale after the run (banner; commit blocked until re-run or acknowledged by rule).
requirements.title: Run review

requirements.desc: Committing a run freezes inputs and outputs, makes qualification state authoritative and posts the ledger entry; it requires an approver who did not prepare the run.
requirements.why: Reproducibility and separation of duties.
requirements.pre: Run Calculated; review opened; no blocking exceptions.
requirements.logic: Single database transaction: mark run and period Committed, write state, post balanced journal entry (expense, payables, withholding, residue), write outbox events.
requirements.out: Committed run; journal entry; RunCommitted event.
requirements.valid: Ledger entry balances; sum of payables plus withholding plus residue equals run total.
requirements.err: Approver equals preparer (refused); invariant fails (transaction rolled back).
requirements.title: Commit with second-person approval

requirements.desc: Every result line stores run id, plan version, rule id, pass, payee position, compact inputs (order line ids or aggregate keys, volume, rate, rank as evaluated, tree snapshot reference), intermediate values and rounding. A full trace is regenerated by replay.
requirements.why: Proving why a commission was calculated; disputes and support cost.
requirements.logic: Return stored compact trace; on demand replay the rule for that payee from the snapshot and expand.
requirements.valid: Trace totals equal line amount.
requirements.err: Snapshot archived to cold storage (asynchronous retrieval).
requirements.perm: Staff with trace permission; distributors see the simplified explanation only (FR-DIST-002).
requirements.title: Per-line provenance and trace

requirements.desc: Re-running a committed period from its snapshot with its plan and settings versions reproduces every line exactly, regardless of later corrections or engine releases flagged compatible.
requirements.why: The core audit property.
requirements.trigger: Replay request or CI differential test.
requirements.logic: Engine version pinned per run; replay executes in a sandbox and compares hash of ordered lines.
requirements.valid: Hash equality.
requirements.err: Engine version retired (must remain runnable for the retention period).
requirements.title: Replay of committed periods

requirements.desc: A restatement is requested with a reason, recalculated in a sandbox copy with corrected inputs, shown as a per-payee and per-bonus diff, approved, and applied as adjustments in the open period. No posting or committed line is edited.
requirements.why: Real errors must be corrected openly.
requirements.logic: Sandbox run; diff; approval by a second person; adjustment lines created in the open run referencing the restatement; statement shows them separately.
requirements.valid: Diff totals equal sum of adjustments.
requirements.err: Approval refused; diff empty (closed with no action).
requirements.perm: Compliance officer requests; Finance approver approves.
requirements.title: Restatement of a committed period

requirements.desc: The open run includes adjustment lines generated from late transactions, clawback netting, approved manual adjustments and restatements, each linked to its origin.
requirements.why: Everything that changes pay flows through a run and the ledger.
requirements.pre: Origins approved where approval is required.
requirements.logic: Generate lines with origin type and id; include in control totals by category.
requirements.valid: Each origin consumed once (once-only key).
requirements.err: Origin withdrawn before run (skipped, logged).
requirements.title: Adjustment lines from late transactions and cases

requirements.desc: A calendar can declare provisional payments (weekly advances or estimated pool payouts) that a later final run trues up.
requirements.why: Two hold-out plans pay provisionally; needs a state the MVP lifecycle does not have.
requirements.logic: Provisional run commits and pays; final run computes the final amount and posts the difference.
requirements.valid: Final minus provisional equals true-up per payee.
requirements.err: Negative true-up handled by clawback policy.
requirements.title: Provisional runs with true-up

requirements.desc: Amounts are integers in minor units; intermediate values use fixed-precision decimals; binary floating point is prohibited. Rounding happens once per payout line (default half-up, tenant setting); splits, pools and scaled caps are allocated by largest remainder; unavoidable residue posts to a named account; points-to-currency factors are effective-dated per market.
requirements.why: Cents that do not reconcile break the ledger and trust.
requirements.logic: Decimal library with explicit scale; deterministic tie-break in largest remainder (by fractional part descending, then payee id ascending).
requirements.valid: Sum of parts equals total for every allocation.
requirements.err: Overflow guard on extreme values (run fails).
requirements.title: Money arithmetic

requirements.desc: An append-only journal of balanced entries records what the tenant owes each payee and what payees owe back. Accounts: commission expense, payee payable, withholding payable, payout in transit, settled clearing, clawback receivable, rounding residue, breakage, write-off, and per credit type liability (SDD-09 §2). The platform never records platform-held funds.
requirements.why: Without double entry totals cannot be proved; the word wallet is not used.
requirements.pre: Chart of ledger accounts provisioned per tenant and market.
requirements.trigger: Run commit, payout instruction, settlement, return, clawback, write-off, adjustment.
requirements.logic: Posting rules per event type; entry rejected unless debits equal credits; each entry carries idempotency key, run or case reference and approver; no update or delete.
requirements.valid: Balanced; idempotency key unique.
requirements.err: Duplicate key returns existing entry; unbalanced entry rejected (alert).
requirements.perm: System only; humans act through approved cases.
requirements.title: Double-entry obligations ledger

requirements.desc: A payee's payable, in-transit and receivable balances are sums of postings; nothing is stored as an editable balance. Displayed as earnings balance owed by the tenant.
requirements.why: Balances that can be edited cannot be audited.
requirements.logic: Aggregate by account; cached projection rebuilt from postings and verified nightly.
requirements.valid: Projection equals sum of postings.
requirements.err: Mismatch (projection rebuilt; alert).
requirements.title: Derived payee balances

requirements.desc: Per bonus type the tenant chooses order-line clawback against future earnings or restatement; the resulting amount posts to the payee's clawback receivable and is netted in later runs; the platform never initiates a debit from a distributor's bank account.
requirements.why: The policy decides who bears the cost of a refund; the two methods give different money.
requirements.pre: Policy set per bonus type (default order-line).
requirements.trigger: Refund, return or chargeback after payout.
requirements.logic: Order-line: reverse the commission lines whose source is the order. Restatement: sandbox recalculation of the original period for affected payees. Post receivable; net against payable in the next run up to the available amount; remainder carried.
requirements.out: Clawback lines; receivable postings; statement lines.
requirements.valid: Receivable never exceeds amounts previously paid on the affected lines (order-line) or the restated difference (restatement).
requirements.err: Payee has no future earnings (receivable ages; write-off rule).
requirements.perm: Policy set by Finance manager with approval.
requirements.title: Clawback policy and receivables

requirements.desc: Clawback receivables below a tenant threshold or older than an age limit may be written off with a reason and approval; the posting moves the amount to the write-off account.
requirements.why: Receivables that will never be recovered should not sit forever.
requirements.trigger: Finance proposes a write-off (single or batch with preview).
requirements.logic: Case with approval; posting on approval.
requirements.valid: Amount not above receivable.
requirements.err: Above threshold without second approver.
requirements.perm: Finance manager proposes; Finance approver approves.
requirements.title: Write-off with approval

requirements.desc: At period end a journal export maps ledger accounts to the tenant's chart of accounts and is delivered by file and API; the tenant's ERP stays the general ledger.
requirements.why: Building a general ledger duplicates what every tenant has.
requirements.trigger: Period Committed or Closed; manual request.
requirements.logic: Aggregate postings by mapped account and dimension; lines reference run ids; export is itself recorded and re-downloadable.
requirements.valid: Export balances.
requirements.err: Unmapped account (export blocked with list).
requirements.title: General-ledger journal export

requirements.desc: Credit types with value, expiry, redemption scope and tax-treatment flag; balances are liabilities per type; expiry posts a reversal and notifies the holder in advance. The liability account type exists from MVP.
requirements.why: Thirteen of 21 plans pay non-cash rewards.
requirements.trigger: Run awards credits; redemption event from commerce; expiry job.
requirements.logic: Postings to credit liability; redemption hook API.
requirements.valid: Redemption not above balance.
requirements.err: Expired credit redemption refused.
requirements.title: Non-cash rewards ledger

requirements.desc: Rate table with source and time; conversion performed once at a defined step; statements show original and converted amounts and the rate. MVP is one currency per tenant market.
requirements.why: A plan paying on volume in several currencies is ambiguous without a defined conversion step.
requirements.logic: Conversion pass; stale rate blocks conversion.
requirements.valid: Rate not older than policy.
requirements.err: Stale rate.
requirements.title: Multi-currency with effective-dated rates

requirements.desc: Payable balances above the minimum and not on hold are gathered into a batch per market, provider and currency. States: Draft, Reviewed, Approved, Instructing, Partially settled, Settled, Failed, Cancelled. Preparer and approver differ.
requirements.why: Wrong money is the worst failure.
requirements.pre: Period Committed; provider configured and eligible.
requirements.logic: Select payees; exclude holds (bank-detail cooling-off, duplicate case, missing tax profile where required, tenant hold); show totals and exclusions; approval with step-up; on approval create instructions.
requirements.valid: Batch total equals sum of instruction amounts; each instruction not above payee payable.
requirements.err: Approver equals preparer; provider not eligible; payee balance changed since draft (line recalculated, batch back to Draft).
requirements.perm: Payout officer prepares; Finance approver approves.
requirements.title: Payout batch lifecycle

requirements.desc: A provider-adapter interface (submit, query status, parse settlement report, verify webhook) with one adapter per payout provider and a bank-file adapter per file format. Tenants bring their own provider accounts; credentials are stored encrypted per tenant.
requirements.why: Mainstream providers restrict MLM merchants; no dependence on a single provider.
requirements.logic: Adapter maps instruction to provider request; stores provider reference; bank-file adapter produces a file for manual upload and accepts a result file.
requirements.valid: Provider on the tenant's allow-list for the market.
requirements.err: Provider rejects batch (retry failed lines only); credentials invalid (batch paused).
requirements.perm: System; Tenant admin manages provider configuration.
requirements.title: Provider adapters and bank-file fallback

requirements.desc: Each instruction carries an idempotency key and signature and is sent from a transactional outbox; a retry after timeout sends the same key so that at most one payment results.
requirements.why: Retried instructions must not pay twice.
requirements.logic: Ledger posting payable to in-transit and outbox row in one transaction; dispatcher sends with exponential backoff; ambiguous outcomes resolved by status query before any re-send.
requirements.valid: Signature verifies; key unique per instruction.
requirements.err: Timeout (status query, then retry with same key); permanent rejection (state Failed, amount returned to payable).
requirements.title: Signed, idempotent payout instructions through an outbox

requirements.desc: Provider webhooks and settlement reports are matched to instructions; settled amounts clear in-transit; returned payments move the amount back to payee payable and open a case; unmatched items go to an exceptions queue.
requirements.why: Nobody is paid twice or not at all.
requirements.logic: Idempotent inbound event handling; post settlement or return entries; daily reconciliation totals per provider; period moves to Paid when all instructions are terminal.
requirements.valid: Amount equals instruction amount (differences are exceptions).
requirements.err: Unknown reference; amount mismatch; duplicate webhook (acknowledged without change).
requirements.title: Settlement reconciliation and returned payments

requirements.desc: Bank details are stored as encrypted versions. A new or changed version requires re-authentication, notifies the previous contact, and starts a cooling-off before the first payout to it; payouts due inside the cooling-off are held.
requirements.why: Bank-detail change is a classic payout-fraud vector.
requirements.trigger: Payee or agent submits new details.
requirements.logic: Validate format per market; create version; notify old and new contacts; set cooling-off-until; signal when many payees change to the same account.
requirements.valid: Format valid; account holder name matches payee where the market pack requires.
requirements.err: Re-authentication failed; details shared with other payees above threshold (case).
requirements.perm: Payee self-service; Support agent only through a case with evidence.
requirements.title: Bank-detail versions and change controls

requirements.desc: For each tenant and market the platform records the payment and payout providers, approval date, approved business description and who holds funds; go-live is blocked without it.
requirements.why: Provider eligibility for MLM merchants is decided per merchant and is a launch blocker.
requirements.pre: Provider approval obtained by the tenant.
requirements.logic: Store; show on the launch checklist; reminder before expiry or review dates.
requirements.valid: Evidence attached.
requirements.err: Missing evidence (go-live blocked).
requirements.title: Provider eligibility record

requirements.desc: A market-level minimum payout threshold keeps small payables until they accumulate; holds can be placed on a payee by rule or by an authorised user with reason; a dormant balance report lists payables with no successful payout for a configurable time.
requirements.why: Fees make tiny payouts uneconomic; unclaimed balances may become liabilities.
requirements.logic: Excluded payees listed with reason in the batch; holds are dated events with release.
requirements.valid: Hold has reason and owner.
requirements.err: None specific.
requirements.perm: Payout officer; Compliance officer for holds.
requirements.title: Minimum payout, holds and dormant balances

requirements.desc: Per payee: residency status, tax identifier (stored in the sensitive store, masked on display), entity type and prior-year totals per payer where a rule needs them.
requirements.why: Withholding changes the net amount on every payout line.
requirements.trigger: Payee completes the profile or staff updates through a case.
requirements.logic: Validate format per market pack; version the profile; missing id flags the payee for the higher rate where a rule sets one.
requirements.valid: Identifier format.
requirements.err: Invalid format; missing profile (payout hold if the pack requires).
requirements.title: Payee tax profile

requirements.desc: Effective-dated, market-scoped rules define rate, threshold, threshold basis, payee conditions and the rate when the tax id is missing. Withholding is computed after gross commission and before payout instruction, shown as a separate statement line and posted to a withholding liability. No rate or threshold is built into the platform; values come from the market pack confirmed by a tax adviser.
requirements.why: Mandatory for the tenant as payer in the candidate markets.
requirements.pre: Market pack with tax rules at counsel-confirmed status, or written risk acceptance.
requirements.in: Payee tax profile; gross amount; rule set for the pay date.
requirements.logic: Select applicable rule; compute withholding on the taxable base; round per rule; write tax line; ledger posting at commit.
requirements.valid: Gross equals net plus withholding per payee.
requirements.err: No rule for market and date (zero withholding with exception flag for review).
requirements.perm: Rules maintained in market packs; tenant Finance manager reviews.
requirements.title: Withholding rules per market

requirements.desc: At year end totals per payee per form type are validated (missing tax ids listed), forms generated in the market's format, distributed to payees and exported for the tenant's filing tool.
requirements.why: Annual reporting duty of the payer.
requirements.pre: Tax year closed in the ledger.
requirements.logic: Totals from tax lines and postings; form templates in the market pack; regeneration creates a new version, never overwrites.
requirements.valid: Form totals equal ledger totals.
requirements.err: Missing tax ids (listed; forms for those payees held).
requirements.title: Year-end statements

requirements.desc: One case model serves genealogy changes, duplicates, disputes, manual adjustments, restatements, returned payments, bank-detail exceptions, grievances and privacy requests: type, subject, reason code, evidence, state, assignments, approvals, deadlines and an immutable event history.
requirements.why: Every exceptional change needs reason, evidence and approver in one place.
requirements.persona: Support agent; Commission analyst; Compliance officer
requirements.pre: User has permission for the case type.
requirements.trigger: User or system opens a case.
requirements.logic: Type-specific workflow and policy checks; SLA timers from market pack or tenant setting; effect preview before approval.
requirements.valid: Reason code from the type's list.
requirements.err: Missing evidence where required.
requirements.title: Case framework

requirements.desc: A manual adjustment is a case with reason code and evidence; above a tenant threshold it needs a second approver; nobody approves their own; adjustments to the approver's own or declared related accounts, or to accounts created within a configurable number of days, are blocked or escalated.
requirements.why: Manual adjustment is the main insider-fraud vector.
requirements.logic: Policy checks; effect preview; on approval the adjustment enters the open run as a line (FR-COMP-010).
requirements.valid: Amount non-zero; payee in tenant.
requirements.err: Self-approval; related account; threshold exceeded without second approver.
requirements.perm: Commission analyst proposes; Finance approver approves.
requirements.title: Manual adjustments with thresholds and second approver

requirements.desc: A distributor opens a dispute from a statement line; the trace is attached automatically; states Opened, Under review, Resolved upheld, Resolved not upheld; response time tracked per market where required.
requirements.why: Disputes resolved with facts instead of hours of tracing.
requirements.logic: Create case with trace; analyst resolves; upheld leads to adjustment or restatement request; outcome and explanation sent to the distributor.
requirements.valid: One open dispute per line.
requirements.err: Dispute window passed (tenant setting; explanation shown).
requirements.perm: Line owner opens; Commission analyst resolves.
requirements.title: Commission dispute from a statement line

requirements.desc: Per pay period and per person: lines grouped by position and bonus, gross, withholding, clawbacks and adjustments as separate lines, net, payout status, rank used, period, and the disclosure link where one is published. No income projection appears anywhere.
requirements.why: The statement is where distributor trust is won or lost.
requirements.logic: Read from committed result lines, tax lines and payout status; cacheable after commit; totals per position and per person.
requirements.valid: Person total equals sum of positions; net equals gross minus withholding minus netted clawbacks plus adjustments.
requirements.err: Period not yet committed (shows status only, no estimates).
requirements.perm: Self only; Support agent with masked data.
requirements.title: Distributor statement

requirements.desc: Each statement line opens a plain-language explanation generated from the trace by template: rule name, base volume, rate, rank used, period, rounding. No other person's personal data appears.
requirements.why: A distributor can trust or dispute a line with facts.
requirements.logic: Template per rule type filled from the compact trace; downline sources shown as counts and aggregates per the visibility policy.
requirements.valid: Explanation amount equals line amount.
requirements.err: Template missing for an extension rule (generic explanation with inputs listed; flagged to implementation).
requirements.title: Line explanation

requirements.desc: Shows paid-as rank and titles for recent periods, the requirements of the current rank with the participant's measured values, and maintenance or grace status. It states facts only; it does not project income or show what could be earned.
requirements.why: Rank ambiguity produces disputes; the honesty policy forbids projections.
requirements.logic: Read state and plan requirements; current open period values are labelled not final.
requirements.valid: Values equal state rows for committed periods.
requirements.err: Plan change in progress (transition notice).
requirements.title: Rank status, factual

requirements.desc: A leader searches their own downline and sees only the fields the visibility policy allows; beyond the depth limit only aggregates.
requirements.why: Leaders help their team without seeing private data.
requirements.logic: FR-GEN-006 enforcement; explains why data is limited.
requirements.valid: Server-side filtering.
requirements.err: Outside downline (not found).
requirements.title: Team view, privacy-limited

requirements.desc: A distributor sees the customers they service with order recency and repeat-order indicator, and customers reassigned to or from them with dates.
requirements.why: Customer-based metrics are the defensible measure of productive activity.
requirements.logic: Read servicing rows and attributed orders; contact fields per tenant policy.
requirements.valid: Only current and past own servicing rows.
requirements.err: None specific.
requirements.title: My customers

requirements.desc: The distributor views masked bank details and tax profile, submits changes with re-authentication, and sees cooling-off status and affected payouts.
requirements.why: Self-service reduces support load while keeping change controls.
requirements.logic: FR-PAY-005 and FR-TAX-001.
requirements.valid: As FR-PAY-005.
requirements.err: As FR-PAY-005.
requirements.title: Bank details and tax profile self-service

requirements.desc: Distributor pages and statements are available in the launch market's languages, with locale-aware numbers and dates, server-rendered small payloads and readable type sizes.
requirements.why: The user base is multilingual with a large share aged 55 and over; statement comprehension depends on language.
requirements.pre: Translations complete for the market pack languages.
requirements.logic: Message catalogues; no text in images; statement core readable without client-side scripts where possible.
requirements.valid: No untranslated key in release.
requirements.err: Missing translation falls back to market default language and is logged.
requirements.title: Localisation and low-bandwidth delivery

requirements.desc: Transactional notifications by email and, where the tenant configures a provider, SMS or messaging: statement ready, payout sent or returned, bank details changed, dispute update, plan-change notice, credit expiry. In-app inbox mirrors them.
requirements.why: Security notices and plan-change notices are required by other rules.
requirements.logic: Outbox-driven; per-channel preferences except mandatory security notices; delivery status stored.
requirements.valid: Template exists in recipient locale or default.
requirements.err: Delivery failure (retry; fallback channel for security notices).
requirements.title: Notifications

requirements.desc: Leaders see customers served, repeat-order rate, returns and time to first customer for their team within visibility limits. No recruit leaderboards.
requirements.why: Productivity defined by retail customers, not recruits; unvalidated need.
requirements.logic: Aggregates from attributed orders.
requirements.valid: Aggregates only beyond depth limit.
requirements.err: None specific.
requirements.title: Leader dashboard on customers served

requirements.desc: Access, correction, erasure and portability requests are logged, identity-verified, fulfilled within the market deadline and closed with the legal basis for anything retained.
requirements.why: The platform is a processor with direct duties in some markets.
requirements.pre: Request received through the portal, public form or tenant staff.
requirements.logic: Privacy case with deadline; access export assembled from personal-data map; erasure per FR-PRV-002.
requirements.valid: Identity verified.
requirements.err: Verification failed; deadline approaching (escalation).
