requirements.title: Data-subject requests

requirements.desc: Where ledger and tax retention applies, erasure replaces identity fields with a pseudonym and deletes sensitive documents; postings, result lines and relationships are retained.
requirements.why: Ledger integrity and retention law versus erasure rights.
requirements.logic: Irreversible replacement of identity fields; key destruction for the sensitive store entries; audit of the operation.
requirements.valid: No identity field remains in primary or read models; backups age out per retention.
requirements.err: Open payable balance or legal hold (erasure deferred with explanation).
requirements.title: Erasure by pseudonymisation

requirements.desc: Retention period per data class and market; deletion jobs with logs.
requirements.why: Mandatory in some markets from stated dates.
requirements.logic: Scheduled jobs; legal holds respected.
requirements.valid: Schedule exists.
requirements.err: Hold present.
requirements.title: Retention timers

requirements.desc: Per tenant and market the platform stores breach contacts and notification timelines, and can produce the list of affected data subjects and data classes for a given scope.
requirements.why: Processor duty to notify tenants without delay with the facts they need.
requirements.logic: Stored in settings; incident tooling queries audit and data maps.
requirements.valid: At least one contact per tenant.
requirements.err: Missing contact blocks go-live.
requirements.perm: Tenant admin edits; Vendor ops reads.
requirements.title: Breach-notification contacts and runbook data

requirements.desc: Every security-relevant and money-relevant action writes an audit event (actor, action, object, before and after references, tenant, time, request id) to an append-only store separate from the application tables.
requirements.why: Investigation and attestation evidence from day one.
requirements.logic: Written in the same transaction through the outbox to the audit store; hash-chained per tenant; searchable by actor, object and time.
requirements.valid: Chain verification job passes.
requirements.err: Audit store unavailable (events buffered in outbox; money actions blocked if the buffer exceeds a limit).
requirements.perm: Read: Tenant admin, Compliance officer; vendor reads only inside a support session.
requirements.title: Immutable audit log

requirements.desc: Exports of rows containing personal data are limited in size per role, respect visibility rules, and are logged with who, what filter and how many rows.
requirements.why: Mass extraction is a breach path.
requirements.logic: Row cap per role; asynchronous for large exports; watermark with requester id.
requirements.valid: Within cap.
requirements.err: Above cap (refused with path to request a scheduled export).
requirements.title: Export limits and logging

requirements.desc: Versioned REST API under /v1 with OpenAPI description, idempotency keys on writes, cursor pagination, per-key rate limits, and signed outbound webhooks with retries for domain events.
requirements.why: The product is API-first behind any commerce front end.
requirements.logic: Standards in the TRD API requirements.
requirements.valid: Schema validation.
requirements.err: Standard error envelope.
requirements.title: Public API and webhooks

requirements.desc: For each connector and provider: last successful sync, lag, error counts, reconciliation differences; runs are blocked when order sync is behind the cut-off.
requirements.why: A run on partial data pays wrongly.
requirements.logic: Health states Healthy, Behind, Failing with thresholds; alerts.
requirements.valid: Heartbeat fresh.
requirements.err: Connector credentials expired (Failing; guidance).
requirements.title: Integration and sync health

requirements.desc: A documented, versioned export of the tenant's complete data (genealogy history, orders, runs, lines, traces, ledger, cases) in open formats on a schedule to the tenant's storage, with row counts that reconcile.
requirements.why: Analysts will not adopt a platform that hides their data; exit rights lower switching risk.
requirements.pre: Destination configured in the tenant's region.
requirements.logic: Snapshot-consistent export from the replica; manifest with counts and checksums.
requirements.valid: Counts equal source counts at snapshot.
requirements.err: Destination unreachable (retry; alert).
requirements.title: Scheduled export of the full tenant data model

requirements.desc: Dedicated-database tenants get read-only SQL access to a replica schema of their own data.
requirements.why: Buyer expectation set by incumbents; never on shared schema or primary.
requirements.logic: Replica with documented views; credentials per user; query limits.
requirements.valid: Tier dedicated.
requirements.err: Pooled tenant (not available).
requirements.title: Read-only analytical replica for dedicated tenants

requirements.desc: Executive overview (sales, active earners, payout as share of sales, retail share, market view), finance dashboard (payables, in transit, receivables, withholding, failed payouts), analyst home (periods and runs), compliance overview (report figures, guardrail warnings, open cases). Each figure has a stated definition.
requirements.why: Different roles need different homes; owners rely on staff for numbers today.
requirements.logic: Read models refreshed on commit and on ingestion; definitions in the reporting catalogue.
requirements.valid: Figures reconcile with committed runs and ledger.
requirements.err: Partial data banner when sync is behind.
requirements.title: Role dashboards

requirements.desc: Every large table supports server-side filtering, sorting, column choice, saved views per user and export within limits.
requirements.why: Reviews of incumbents cite cumbersome reporting.
requirements.logic: Stored per user; shareable within role.
requirements.valid: Columns permitted for role.
requirements.err: None specific.
requirements.title: Operational lists with saved views

requirements.desc: Import of genealogy history, positions, rank and title history, carry balances, counters, open balances and bank and tax profiles from a legacy system through a mapping workspace with validation reports.
requirements.why: Switching cost is the barrier every entrant must lower.
requirements.logic: Staged load; validation (cycles, orphans, totals); opening qualification state and opening ledger entry posted with approval.
requirements.valid: Opening ledger balances equal legacy balances by payee.
requirements.err: Cycles or orphans (listed; load blocked).
requirements.perm: Implementation consultant; opening entry approved by tenant Finance approver.
requirements.title: History import

requirements.desc: For at least one full period the new platform's results are compared per payee and per bonus with the legacy system's payouts; go-live requires differences of zero or each difference explained and approved.
requirements.why: Proof that the new system pays the same is the switching lever and the go-live safety.
requirements.pre: History imported; legacy payout file for the period.
requirements.logic: Simulation-harness run; diff report; each difference classified (rule, data, rounding) and resolved or accepted with approver.
requirements.valid: Unexplained differences equal zero for sign-off.
requirements.err: Legacy file lacks bonus detail (payee-level comparison only, flagged).
requirements.perm: Implementation consultant; Finance approver signs off.
requirements.title: Parallel-run reconciliation

requirements.desc: A separate application area for vendor staff: tenant list with region, tier and health; provisioning; support-session requests; market-pack maintenance. It shows no tenant business data outside an approved session.
requirements.why: Vendor staff are a distinct, high-risk role.
requirements.logic: Separate identity realm; all actions audited to a vendor audit log and, for tenant-affecting actions, to the tenant's log.
requirements.valid: No tenant data without session.
requirements.err: Attempt to open tenant data without session (blocked, logged).
requirements.title: Vendor operations console

requirements.desc: A summary of the deterministic run diff in plain language, citing the lines and inputs it summarises.
requirements.why: Analysts trace variances by hand; only after deterministic diff reports exist.
requirements.logic: Model receives only the diff; output must cite line ids; never writes to plans or ledger.
requirements.valid: Every figure in the summary matches a cited value.
requirements.err: Citation check fails (summary discarded).
requirements.title: Run variance explainer

requirements.desc: For implementation staff: drafts plan rules and golden cases from a plan document; every rule is confirmed by a person and by golden tests.
requirements.why: Implementation cost decides margins; untested idea.
requirements.logic: Draft only; human sign-off; simulation required.
requirements.valid: No draft can be activated without FR-PLN-006 passing.
requirements.err: Unsupported mechanism (listed for extension).
requirements.title: Plan-document-to-configuration assistant (internal)

requirements.desc: A self-hosted installation runs under a signed licence file stating licensee, edition, enabled modules, payee band, market packs, support and update entitlement and expiry. The application verifies the signature offline at start and daily. It never stops calculating or paying because a licence lapsed: on expiry it keeps running, shows a notice to administrators, and stops accepting new engine versions and market-pack updates.
requirements.why: Founder decision DEC-17: the product is sold both as hosted SaaS and as a licensed self-hosted edition. A lapse must never cause wrong or missed pay.
requirements.pre: Licence issued by the vendor for the installation id.
requirements.trigger: Installation, start-up, daily check, licence renewal.
requirements.logic: Verify signature with the embedded public key; compare installation id and limits; compute entitlement; expose state Active, Grace, Lapsed; write audit events; no network call is required.
requirements.out: Entitlement state; administrator notice; audit event.
requirements.valid: Signature valid; installation id matches; clock rollback detected by monotonic checkpoint.
requirements.err: Invalid signature (application starts in read-only mode with export enabled); payee band exceeded (notice and report only; no blocking of runs).
requirements.perm: Tenant admin installs a licence; nobody can edit entitlement.
requirements.title: Licence entitlement for the self-hosted edition

requirements.desc: Application releases, engine versions and market packs for self-hosted installations are delivered as signed packages that the licensee applies deliberately. Each package states its version, compatibility, migrations and, for market packs, the basis status of every rule. An installation shows how far it is behind and which known defects affect the version it runs.
requirements.why: An unpatched self-hosted engine or an out-of-date tax rule pays people wrongly; the vendor cannot fix it remotely.
requirements.trigger: Licensee downloads a package or the installation checks the update feed (optional, outbound only).
requirements.logic: Verify signature and compatibility; run golden datasets and a replay sample against the new engine before it can be activated; apply migrations; committed runs keep their pinned engine version; market-pack changes take effect from their effective dates only.
requirements.out: Installed version; update log; advisories list.
requirements.valid: Package signed by the vendor; target version reachable from current version.
requirements.err: Golden or replay check fails (update not activated, report produced); migration fails (automatic rollback to the pre-update snapshot).
requirements.perm: Tenant admin with second approver for engine and market-pack updates.
requirements.title: Signed updates and market-pack distribution

requirements.desc: The self-hosted edition installs as a single-tenant deployment from a documented package (containers with a reference configuration), with a preflight check, health diagnostics, backup and restore tooling and a support bundle that contains configuration and logs but no personal data, bank details or secrets. Vendor support works only through licensee-approved sessions or on the bundle.
requirements.why: The licensee operates the system; the vendor has no access by default.
requirements.in: Configuration; infrastructure endpoints (database, object storage, identity provider, mail).
requirements.logic: Preflight verifies versions, extensions, encryption settings, time sync and backup target; diagnostics page shows job queues, outbox age, replication, last backup and restore-test date; support bundle generator redacts by allow-list.
requirements.valid: Bundle passes the redaction test before it can be exported.
requirements.err: Preflight failure (installation refuses to proceed with the list); backup target unreachable (alert; runs can be blocked by setting).
requirements.title: Self-hosted installation, diagnostics and support bundle

stories.want: to see the tree exactly as it was on any past date
stories.so: I can explain a past payout after later corrections
stories.value: Reproducibility of paid history; faster dispute handling.
stories.pre: Relationship history exists; analyst has genealogy read.
stories.main: Open the genealogy explorer; search a position; set the as-of date; optionally set known-at; expand branches; open the run that used this tree.
stories.alt: Read model rebuilding: depth-limited view from the system of record with a notice.

stories.want: to file a sponsor-change request with reason and evidence
stories.so: changes are reviewed instead of edited directly
stories.main: Open the participant; choose Request genealogy change; pick change or correction; choose proposed parent; attach evidence; submit.
stories.alt: Outside the plan's change window: rejected with the rule shown, or routed to the exception approver if the plan allows.

stories.want: to approve or reject genealogy corrections and see which committed periods they affect
stories.so: corrections do not silently change paid history
stories.value: Paid history changes only through an open, approved path.
stories.main: Open the case; read evidence; review affected periods and estimated impact; approve or reject with reason; system applies rows and queues read-model rebuild.
stories.alt: Affects committed periods: choose adjust in open period or raise a restatement request.

stories.want: to hold several positions and see one combined statement
stories.so: my earnings are clear even with several business centres
stories.value: Trust in pay for multi-position plans.
stories.main: Open Earnings; choose period; read totals per person; expand each position.
stories.alt: Single position: no grouping level shown.

stories.want: to search my downline and see only the fields the company allows
stories.so: I can help my team without seeing private data
stories.main: Open Team; search by name or id; open a member; see permitted fields; expand lazily.
stories.alt: Beyond the depth limit: counts and volume aggregates only, with an explanation.

stories.want: to run a period, review variance against the last run and send it for approval
stories.so: mistakes are caught before money moves
stories.main: Open Periods and runs; start calculation; watch progress; open review; inspect variance, movers and exceptions; fix inputs and re-run if needed; request commit.
stories.alt: Sync behind: calculation blocked with last sync time. Run fails: resume from snapshot.

stories.want: to approve a committed run only if I did not prepare it
stories.so: no single person can release payouts
stories.main: Open approvals; read review summary; pass step-up; commit.
stories.alt: Approver is preparer: refused; eligible approvers listed.

stories.want: late orders after commit to land in a queue and post as adjustments
stories.so: committed periods stay reproducible
stories.main: Open late-transaction queue; review items and estimated effects; accept default handling; adjustments appear in the open run.
stories.alt: Material item: raise a restatement request instead.

stories.want: to request a restatement with a reason and see the diff before approval
stories.so: real errors can be corrected openly
stories.main: Open Cases; create restatement; system recalculates in a sandbox; review diff per payee and bonus; send for approval; adjustments post in the open period.
stories.alt: Diff empty: case closed with no action.

stories.want: to compare a new plan version with the current one on last period's data, payee by payee
stories.so: I know who gains and loses before release
stories.main: Open the draft; choose Simulate; pick period; read totals, distribution and payee-level differences; export.
stories.alt: No full historical period available: activation remains blocked.

stories.want: to configure a cap with scope, base, method and see who is cut
stories.so: the cap behaves as the plan document says
stories.value: Caps applied to the right lines.
stories.main: Open caps; set scope, base, rate, method, priority, residue rule; preview on a period; save.
stories.alt: Overlapping caps: precedence must be stated.

stories.want: to open any statement line and see how it was calculated
stories.so: I can trust or dispute it with facts
stories.main: Open statement; tap a line; read rule, base, rate, rank, period, rounding; optionally open a dispute.
stories.alt: Extension rule without template: generic explanation listing inputs.

stories.want: to see the full calculation trace for a payout line
stories.so: I can answer pay questions without engineering
stories.main: Search the payee; open statement; open line trace; read source orders, plan version, rule and intermediate values.
stories.alt: Snapshot in cold storage: trace requested and delivered asynchronously.

stories.want: the sum of payout lines, residues and withholding to equal the run total to the minor unit
stories.so: the ledger reconciles
stories.main: Open ledger for the period; compare control totals; open residue account.
stories.alt: Projection mismatch: rebuilt automatically and alerted.

stories.want: a journal export mapped to our chart of accounts at period end
stories.so: our ERP stays the general ledger
stories.main: Open Ledger and exports; choose period; generate; download or fetch by API.
stories.alt: Unmapped account: export blocked with the list.

stories.want: failed and returned payments to come back to a queue and be re-instructed safely
stories.so: nobody is paid twice or not at all
stories.main: Open reconciliation; see settled, returned, failed, unmatched; open a returned item; fix cause through a case; include in next batch.
stories.alt: Provider rejects whole batch: retry failed lines only.

stories.want: to be told when my bank details change, and payouts to wait before using new details
stories.so: a takeover cannot redirect my money
stories.main: Open Payment details; submit new details; re-authenticate; see cooling-off date; receive notices on old and new contacts.
stories.alt: Payout due inside cooling-off: held, shown on statement.

stories.want: withholding applied to payees who meet the market rule and year-end statements produced
stories.so: we meet our withholding duty
stories.value: Mandatory duty of the payer. Example pack: Malaysia (rate and threshold to be confirmed by a tax adviser).
stories.main: Review tax rules; run period; see withholding lines; at year end generate forms; export.
stories.alt: Missing tax ids: listed; forms held for those payees.

stories.want: the higher rate applied when no tax id is held
stories.so: we meet the rule in force
stories.value: Mandatory duty. Example pack: India (provision and rates to be confirmed by a chartered accountant).
stories.pre: Market pack rule with missing-id rate.
stories.main: Run period; payees without tax id carry the higher rate; statement shows it.
stories.alt: Tax id supplied later: applies from the next pay date; no retroactive change without the market's rule.

stories.want: to choose a clawback policy per bonus type and see receivables and write-offs
stories.so: refunds are recovered consistently
stories.main: Open settings; choose policy per bonus; view receivables ageing; propose write-offs; get approval.
stories.alt: Payee has no future earnings: receivable ages until written off.

stories.want: to define participant types and order purposes
stories.so: the retail-customer share is measured on the right population
stories.main: Define types with flags; define purpose requirement; approve.
stories.alt: Type change for a participant: effective-dated; past orders keep labels.

stories.want: orders, refunds and customers from our Shopify or WooCommerce store to flow in automatically and idempotently
stories.so: we do not re-key orders
stories.main: Install connector; authorise store; map products to volume; watch sync health.
stories.alt: Unknown product: order held in the exception queue.

stories.want: to reassign a terminated distributor's customers by the company's rule
stories.so: customers keep being served and attribution stays correct
stories.main: Terminate through case; system applies reassignment rule; review list; override single customers through a case if needed.
stories.alt: No eligible target: customers assigned to the company.

stories.want: reports on retail-customer share, personal-consumption share and payout sources per period
stories.so: I can answer a regulator or counsel from the system
stories.value: The differentiator candidate; the demand test of MVP-A.
stories.main: Open Compliance reports; choose period range; create snapshot; read figures with method notes; open a figure to its rows; export.
stories.alt: Data-quality warnings: shown beside affected figures.

stories.want: an earnings distribution computed from all participants' payouts, including zero earners, and kept with its method
stories.so: our claims are substantiated
stories.main: Create yearly snapshot; read distribution; (V1) draft and publish disclosure.
stories.alt: Partial year: labelled partial and not publishable.

stories.want: the platform to block plan components that pay solely for enrolment in markets that ban them, and tell me why
stories.so: we do not configure an unlawful plan by accident
stories.value: Reduced legal exposure for tenant and vendor.
stories.main: Plan admin saves a rule; guardrail evaluates; blocked with rule id and explanation, or warned with acknowledgement.
stories.alt: Overridable warning: justification and compliance approval recorded.

stories.want: a plan change to move through simulation, compliance review, filing status, notice and an effective date, with a transition report
stories.so: the field is treated fairly and filings are not missed
stories.main: Submit; simulation attached; compliance review; record filing status; set notice; approver schedules activation; transition report produced at first run.
stories.alt: Filing required and missing: blocked.

stories.want: to import history and run old and new systems in parallel with a per-payee difference report
stories.so: go-live happens only when payouts match
stories.main: Map and import history; validate; configure plan; run parallel period; classify differences; obtain sign-off.
stories.alt: Differences outstanding: go-live blocked.

stories.want: to approve or deny a vendor support session and see everything done in it
stories.so: the vendor cannot access our data silently
stories.main: Receive request; read reason and scope; approve for a duration or deny; later read the session report.
stories.alt: No decision before request expiry: auto-denied.

stories.want: to request access to or erasure of my data
stories.so: my privacy rights are honoured
stories.main: Submit request in portal or public form; verify identity; receive export or confirmation; see what is retained and why.
stories.alt: Open payable balance or legal hold: erasure deferred with explanation.

rules.rule: A participant may own one or more positions; volume and qualification are evaluated per position unless the plan says per participant
Sponsor and placement relationships are separate, each with valid-from and valid-to dates and recorded time, and are never updated in place
A change takes effect from an approved current or future date and never alters committed periods
A correction records the original valid date; committed periods it affects are flagged and handled by the restatement policy (BR-PER-05)
Change windows and approval requirements for sponsor and placement changes are plan-version parameters
Placement into a binary or matrix position is serialised per target leg; the tie-break is deterministic and recorded
Termination changes position status; the tree structure is not modified to implement compression, roll-up or breakaway
Re-parenting of a terminated position's downline, if the plan requires it, is a dated change event with a stated rule per plan version
Duplicate-account suspicion blocks activation pending review where the tenant enables it
Succession, divorce division and sale of a distributorship are transfers of position ownership with documents and approval; history stays with the position
Reinstatement is an event on the same position; rank and placement after return follow a rule per plan version
Authorisation checks use the path read model when current and fall back to the system of record when it is stale; a stale read model never widens access
Each plan defines one or more calendars and the time zone of each cut-off
A transaction is assigned to a period by its defined crediting event (payment, shipment or end of cooling-off). UNRESOLVED: which event (D-R1)
Period states are Open, Calculating, Calculated, Committed, Paid, Closed; inputs and outputs are frozen at Committed
Transactions arriving after Committed post as adjustments in the current open period by default
A restatement reopens nothing: it recalculates a committed period in a sandbox with approval, a reason and a stored diff; paid amounts are corrected by adjustments, never by editing postings
A run is idempotent per tenant, calendar, period and run request id and locked against concurrent runs
A provisional run is paid and later trued up by a final run that posts only the difference
Amounts are held in minor units or fixed-precision decimals; binary floating point is prohibited
Rounding happens once per payout line at a defined step; the rounding mode is a tenant setting with platform default half-up
Splits, pools and scaled caps are allocated so that parts sum exactly to the total (largest remainder; ties by payee id ascending)
Any unavoidable residue posts to a named residue account
Points-to-currency factors are effective-dated per market and shown on statements
A cap has a scope (bonus types), a base expression, a rate, a method (proportional, priority list, per person) and a residue rule
Per-participant constraints are evaluated before company-level caps
Simulation shows, for each cap, the payees affected and amounts removed
Each position has a paid-as rank per period and a highest-achieved title, stored separately
Qualification windows (period-end, rolling n periods, per order) are declared per requirement
Cross-period state is an output of a committed run and an input to the next; it is never edited directly
Carry-forward has optional conditions, caps and expiry
Several rank ladders may exist per participant
Participant types are tenant-defined with flags: can earn, counts as end customer, can sponsor, can hold positions
Type changes are effective-dated and do not re-label past orders
Every participant order carries a purpose (resale, personal use, unspecified) where the market or tenant requires it
Each customer has one serviced-by relationship at a time, effective-dated
Attribution, buyer type, purpose and line volumes are fixed on the order at ingestion
On termination of the servicing distributor, customers are reassigned by a tenant rule with notice
Fractional roll-ups of customer volume are plan parameters
Every order records the buyer's participant type at the time of the order (replaces the original binary buyer type, IC-14)
An order is unique per tenant, source system and source order id; replays with the same content are no-ops
A run may not start while order sync lag exceeds the tenant threshold at cut-off
Volume per order line comes from a product-to-volume map effective at the crediting event time
Reversal of volume is proportional to the returned lines (see BR-RET-01)
Returns reverse volume per returned line, not per order
An exchange of equal value flagged as such does not reverse and re-credit volume
Restocking fees reduce the refund; their effect on volume is a tenant setting
Whether a reversal changes a closed period or posts an adjustment is a tenant policy within platform rules. UNRESOLVED legally (D-R2)
A chargeback is treated like a refund for volume and pay
Default clawback method is order-line clawback against future earnings; restatement is available per bonus type
Clawback receivables below a tenant threshold may be written off with approval
The platform never initiates a debit from a distributor's bank account
Withholding rules are effective-dated and market-scoped: rate, threshold, threshold basis, payee conditions
Withholding is computed after gross commission and before payout instruction and posts to a withholding liability
Missing tax id applies the market's higher rate where the law sets one
Year-end statements are generated per market form with thresholds per tax year
Payout batches have separate preparer and approver and an audit trail (reconstructed from MH-REQ-02)
Statements itemise each payout line by source (reconstructed from MH-REQ-09)
New or changed bank details trigger re-authentication, notice to the previous contact, and a cooling-off before the first payout
Returned payments move the amount back to the payee's payable balance and open a case
Payout instructions carry idempotency keys and are signed
Payment and payout providers must be confirmed eligible for the tenant's business type in the market before go-live
Payables below the market's minimum payout accumulate; holds are dated events with reason and owner
Every journal entry balances (sum of debits equals sum of credits) and carries an idempotency key, origin reference and approver where a human decided
Postings are append-only; balances are sums of postings and are never edited
The ledger records obligations of the tenant, never funds held by the platform; the word wallet is not used for anything the platform records
Every manual adjustment has a reason code, evidence and a case
Approvals above a tenant threshold need a second approver; nobody approves what they prepared
Adjustments to accounts of the approver, declared relatives or accounts created in the last n days are blocked or escalated
A commission dispute has states opened, under review, resolved upheld, resolved not upheld, and a response time per market where required
Blocked: a payout component whose only trigger is enrolling a person, in markets that ban it
Blocked: fees or deposits from participants where the market prohibits them
Warned and logged: starter kits carrying commissionable volume; personal-consumption share above a tenant threshold
Reported: retail-customer share, payout-source mix, earnings distribution
Guardrail overrides need a written justification from the tenant and are visible in compliance reports
A run uses exactly one plan version, chosen by effective date (original catalogue)
Currency conversion follows a tenant policy with an effective-dated rate table (original catalogue, narrowed by BR-MNY)
Each new plan version declares transition rules for titles, carry balances, streaks and one-time flags
A version cannot be activated without a simulation on at least one full historical period
Where a market requires a filing, activation is blocked until the filing status is recorded
Field notice period before activation is a tenant setting
Tenant-specific code branches are prohibited; extensions are expressions or platform-reviewed modules available to all tenants
Every plan version and every engine release must reproduce its golden datasets exactly
Each credit type has value, expiry, redemption scope and tax treatment flag
Expiry posts a reversal of the credit liability and notifies the holder in advance
Vendor staff have no standing access to tenant data; access is a tenant-approved, time-boxed session, logged and visible to the tenant
Payout approvers, tenant admins and vendor staff use multi-factor authentication
Exports and API extraction of personal data are limited, logged and attributed
The tenant id is taken from the authenticated session and enforced in the data layer; it is never accepted from the client
A grant of an admin or approver role needs a second admin; a user cannot grant permissions they do not hold
Separation of duties is evaluated from recorded actor ids on the object, not from role names
Audit events are append-only, stored separately from application tables and hash-chained per tenant
Downline visibility follows a field-by-depth policy enforced on the server (original rule made specific by GAP-012)
Erasure requests pseudonymise payee identity in the ledger rather than deleting postings, where retention law allows
Breach-notification timelines and contacts are configured per market and per tenant
Prospect data entered by a distributor is private to that distributor by default
Personal data, backups and exports stay in the tenant's configured region
An archived tenant is read-only; data is retained per law and then deleted
Each data class has a retention period per market; deletion jobs are logged
A tenant can export its complete data in a documented open format at any time
An overlay export may not contain names, contact details, addresses, identity numbers or bank data; a file with such columns is rejected whole
rules.basis: Phase A validate_export.py; P4 data terms

rules.rule: Imported amounts are integers in minor units; participant ids are pseudonymous
Every compliance figure records the mapping version that produced it
A re-import supersedes, never deletes, the earlier batch
Every compliance figure stores its population, method version and inputs and can be recomputed identically
Every market-pack rule stores its basis and basis status (screening, primary read, counsel-confirmed)
The product contains no income projection, potential-earnings calculator or recruit leaderboard
Wherever earnings are shown to participants or prospects, the published disclosure is linked when one exists
Enrolment and shipping are restricted to markets the tenant has opened (original catalogue)
Where the market pack requires it, enrolment needs acceptance of the current agreement version
Distributor-facing text is delivered in the market's configured languages with locale-aware formats
Opening balances and opening qualification state from a migration are posted once, with approval, and are identifiable as migration entries
Go-live requires a parallel run with zero unexplained differences
No model output may write to plans or the ledger; any AI text that mentions money must cite the lines it summarises
A licence lapse never blocks calculation, commit, payout, statements or export; it only stops new engine versions, market-pack updates and support
Licence verification works offline from a signed file; the product does not require a call to the vendor to run
Releases, engine versions and market packs are signed; an engine update is activated only after golden and replay checks pass on the installation
The self-hosted edition gives the vendor no access path; support uses licensee-approved sessions or a redacted bundle
Both editions are built from one codebase with the same guardrails, honesty policy and ledger invariants; no edition removes them and no source-code edition is offered
